root_cause.text: Use of a non-devm workqueue allocation (create_singlethread_workqueue) combined with devm-managed interrupt handlers created an incorrect cleanup order, allowing a use-after-free when the workqueue is destroyed before the interrupt handlers (which schedule work on that workqueue) are freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description explicitly states: "Driver allocates workqueue and then registers interrupt handlers with devm interface. This means that probe error paths will not use a reversed order, but first destroy the workqueue and then, via devm release handlers, free the interrupt. The interrupt handler schedules work on this exact workqueue, thus if interrupt is hit in this short time window - after destroying workqueue, but before devm() frees the interrupt - the scheduled work will lead to use of freed memory." The diff converts the workqueue to devm_alloc_ordered_workqueue and removes the manual destroy_workqueue calls, fixing the ordering issue.

vuln_statements.explanation: Non-devm workqueue allocation creates a cleanup order mismatch: the workqueue is not managed by devm, so it must be destroyed before devm resources are freed. This is the root cause of the use-after-free.
Manual workqueue destruction in the error path occurs before devm-managed interrupt handlers are freed, leading to use-after-free when those handlers schedule work on the already destroyed workqueue.

Devm-managed interrupt handler registration schedules work on the non-devm workqueue. Because the workqueue is destroyed before the interrupt handler is freed (during devm cleanup), a use-after-free occurs when the handler is later invoked.
